suggestion.reason: A small layout improvement in the PR hub, which f5 has.

topics.title: Branch picker no longer jumps when it opens

suggestion.reason: Removes a visible layout shift in the timeline. f5 has ChatView and ThreadErrorBanner.

topics.summary: ThreadErrorBanner moves into the absolutely positioned overlay that ProviderStatusBanner uses, and stacks with it, so the timeline no longer jumps when an error appears or is dismissed.
topics.title: Thread error banner overlays the timeline instead of shifting the chat

suggestion.reason: A reliability and performance fix for terminals on Windows. Reimplement it in f5's terminal manager, adapting it to f5's process sampling.

topics.summary: Terminal subprocess polling takes one shared process snapshot per tick from the resource monitor, instead of a PowerShell CIM query per terminal every second. Failed snapshots back off exponentially.
topics.title: Terminal process polling no longer spikes CPU on Windows

suggestion.reason: Reliability fix for missing chat content. f5 has the same WebSocket subscription path.

topics.summary: The thread live consumer starts immediately, before the snapshot or replay is read, so early assistant-text events are no longer lost and replies no longer show empty until a reload.
topics.title: Thread subscriptions keep live events that arrive during startup

suggestion.reason: Fixes a visible inconsistency on f5 surfaces: the sidebar, project settings and PR hub.

topics.summary: Automatic icons use the saved project title rather than the grouped display label, so the sidebar, header, search, settings and PR filters show the same icon.
topics.title: Automatic project icons are consistent across surfaces

suggestion.reason: Fixes premature overflow of composer controls at narrow widths. It only applies if f5 measures resting composer controls the same way.

topics.summary: Composer control measurement skips the hidden text width of a deliberately collapsed model label, so other controls no longer go into overflow too early.
topics.title: Narrow composers stop reserving width for a collapsed model label

suggestion.reason: A Windows bug in revealing files from chat file chips, which can also happen in f5.

topics.summary: Converts slashes in Windows paths to backslashes before passing them to Explorer's /select. Before, Explorer read the slashes as switches and silently ignored the selection.
topics.title: Reveal in File Explorer selects the file for forward-slash Windows paths

suggestion.reason: A UX consistency improvement, and it fixes the usage refresh indicator, which f5 has. Port the web parts only.

topics.summary: Replaces assorted loading icons with shared Spinner and RefreshIcon components that respect reduced motion. Usage refresh waits for a fresh rescan and stops when the environment disconnects. The mobile parts don't apply.
topics.title: Loading and refresh feedback uses shared Spinner and RefreshIcon

suggestion.reason: A measurable UX fix to settings navigation.

topics.summary: Settings navigation is no longer lazy-loaded, which removes a blank sidebar of about 560 ms on a cold open of settings.
topics.title: Settings sidebar renders immediately instead of blank

suggestion.reason: Visual fix to the sidebar brand that f5 shows.

topics.summary: Groups the T3 mark and the Code label in a baseline-aligned span instead of using per-platform pixel nudges, so the label no longer shifts across fonts.
topics.title: Sidebar T3 wordmark and Code label align on a shared baseline

suggestion.reason: A timeline and Agents panel status bug for the Antigravity provider, which f5 has. It improves f5's Agents panel without replacing it.

topics.summary: Native Antigravity launches are marked as batches. The timeline counts batches separately from agents and shows idle, stopped or unavailable status instead of a green completed check. The Agents panel stays consistent with the timeline.
topics.title: Idle Antigravity subagent batches no longer show completion checkmarks

suggestion.reason: Measured reliability gain in shared shell lookup, which f5 uses for editor and provider discovery.

topics.summary: resolveCommandPath skips exact duplicate PATH directories and creates one trace span per command lookup instead of one per probed file. On slow Windows machines, this cuts the work that made editor discovery time out.
topics.title: Command lookup skips duplicate PATH entries and traces once per lookup

suggestion.reason: A composer UX improvement, provided f5 has the prompt stash.

topics.summary: When the composer is empty and exactly one prompt is stashed, Cmd+S restores it instead of opening the stash menu. Multiple entries, or images still saving, still open the menu.
topics.title: Cmd+S toggles a single stashed prompt directly

suggestion.reason: A measurable server performance improvement for long threads in f5's projection pipeline, which exists in the fork.

topics.summary: The projection pipeline reads the newest user-message timestamp and the pending approval count in SQL, instead of loading every message and approval row. This speeds up session and checkpoint updates on long threads.
topics.title: Thread summary refreshes no longer load every message body

suggestion.reason: This is a measurable performance improvement for self-hosted web clients.

topics.summary: Hashed Vite build files are served with immutable caching. Other files revalidate with weak ETags and Last-Modified and return 304 when unchanged. Metadata and body come from one file handle.
topics.title: Server caches and streams static web assets

suggestion.reason: Measurable server performance improvement. The projection pipeline files exist in f5.

topics.summary: Each orchestration event now writes its nine projector cursor rows in one upsert inside the existing transaction, instead of nine separate statements.
topics.title: Projector cursor writes batched into one upsert per event

suggestion.reason: A measurable streaming performance fix that also preserves UI state in f5's chat timeline.

topics.summary: Markdown component types stay fixed and read message data from context, so streamed updates no longer reset code blocks, copy state or open details. An unchanged fence makes 1 Shiki call instead of 11.
topics.title: Markdown renderers stay mounted during streaming

suggestion.reason: A measurable memory improvement in f5's OpenCode adapter.

topics.summary: Removes the per-session turns array that kept every version of tool output and that nothing read. Memory drops sharply on large tool outputs.
topics.title: OpenCode adapter stops keeping unused tool output history

suggestion.reason: A measurable reduction in disk use for f5's OpenCode provider logs.

topics.summary: EventNdjsonLogger drops OpenCode tool parts in the running state, which repeat the growing output. A 5.3 MB log becomes 103 KB, and pending and final states are kept.
topics.title: OpenCode native logs skip running tool snapshots

suggestion.reason: Measurable resource saving in chat, diffs and the PR hub.

topics.summary: The shared diff worker pool starts only for code previews and diffs, and is disposed after the last one closes. Opening a chat no longer starts 2–6 workers.
topics.title: Diff workers start only when a code view opens

suggestion.reason: This is a measured performance improvement, and it also fixes incomplete totals for large diffs in f5's checkpoint subsystem.

topics.summary: Automatic checkpoint summaries count lines with NUL-delimited git numstat instead of building and parsing full patches. On-demand diffs still use patches. Totals for patches over 10 MB are no longer incomplete. Upstream measured about 4x faster on its fixture.
topics.title: Checkpoint summaries use git numstat instead of full patches

topics.reason: Already present in f5

suggestion.reason: Measurable composer typing performance improvement in a surface f5 has.

topics.summary: The composer draft store keeps the immutable state and defers the draft walk and JSON serialization (including image bytes) until the debounced write flushes.
topics.title: Typing no longer serializes every saved draft before the debounce

suggestion.reason: Measured server performance improvement in provider ingestion, which f5 shares.

topics.summary: Ingestion reads only the thread ID, title and session with one joined query instead of three queries per buffered assistant-text event. 1,000 events now need 1,000 statements instead of 3,000.
topics.title: Buffered provider events read thread context with one query

suggestion.reason: Measurable terminal performance fix. Reimplement in f5's terminal state, because client-runtime does not exist in f5.

topics.summary: The terminal keeps byte-counted output chunks with cursors, so the web terminal appends only unseen data. It resets only on snapshots, lifecycle changes or real gaps, instead of re-encoding and replaying the 512 KiB buffer on rollover.
topics.title: Terminal stops replaying its whole buffer when output rolls over

suggestion.reason: A measurable reliability and memory improvement for f5's WebSocket orchestration stream. It is already planned in Phase 2.

topics.summary: Each live subscription gets a budget of 1,000 items and 8 MiB. On overflow, the producer stops and the client resyncs from its last applied sequence, so slow clients can no longer grow server memory without limit.
topics.title: Bound slow-client WebSocket event buffers

suggestion.reason: Measured performance gain for large thread lists. f5 has no client-runtime, so it must be reimplemented in f5's thread store.

topics.summary: Aggregate thread lists are built from environment data with weakly cached per-thread values, and project membership maps are reused when unchanged. With 10,000 threads, median update time fell from 41.2 ms to 3.4 ms.
topics.title: Thread list updates do less work

suggestion.reason: This is a measurable performance improvement for terminals. Reimplement it in f5's terminal renderer.

topics.summary: Hidden terminal drawers and panels pause frame scheduling, snapshots, canvas paint and cursor timers, while still parsing output. They refit and repaint on reveal. Includes a zero-size canvas guard.
topics.title: Hidden terminals stop rendering frames

suggestion.reason: Measured streaming performance gain in the f5 timeline. Reimplement it in f5's ChatView and session-logic.

topics.summary: When a streaming assistant message changes only its text, the timeline reuses ordered entries and unchanged rows, including finished tool groups, instead of rebuilding them. Attachment previews stay stable.
topics.title: Timeline reuses rows while assistant text streams

suggestion.reason: A measurable performance improvement in orchestration code that f5 shares.

topics.summary: Reconnect reads the selected thread's events through the aggregate index with bounded replay stats, instead of decoding the global log. In upstream's benchmark, median replay time fell from 21.6 ms to 0.9 ms.
topics.title: Thread reconnect replays only the selected thread's events

suggestion.reason: A measured memory improvement in the OpenCode adapter, which f5 has. The change is small.

topics.summary: The OpenCode adapter no longer keeps tool parts in its per-session part map. In upstream's test, 40 completed tools had kept 20 MiB of output in that map. Tool events and text handling are unchanged.
topics.title: OpenCode stops caching tool parts that nothing reads

suggestion.reason: A measured performance improvement already planned for workstream 2. It needs reimplementing in f5's thread state layer.

topics.summary: The detail stream ends when its last consumer leaves. A five-minute idle cache keeps the state and replay cursor, so a quick return resumes without another snapshot download.
topics.title: Closed threads stop their live streams but keep a warm cache

suggestion.reason: Polishes the composer update notice (planned Phase 14).

topics.summary: The idle server update notice uses a download icon. Its actions stay inline down to 320px, and the title truncates instead of crowding them.
topics.title: Server update notice uses a download icon and keeps actions inline

suggestion.reason: Measured sidebar performance gain. It needs reimplementing in f5's terminal state layer, because upstream builds on client-runtime.

topics.summary: Builds one ordered terminal index per snapshot and reuses unchanged thread groups. With 1,000 threads, a terminal change no longer rescans the full list per thread. Upstream measured the median selector time going from 1.05 ms to 0.14 ms.
topics.title: Terminal session selectors reuse one metadata index per snapshot

suggestion.reason: A measured performance improvement in f5's existing orchestration reactor.

topics.summary: ProviderCommandReactor uses thread-shell queries at 14 metadata call sites, such as approvals and session stop. On a 2,000-message thread, the query median fell from 30 ms to 0.5 ms with no message bodies decoded.
topics.title: Provider metadata commands skip full thread history reads

suggestion.reason: A sidebar emphasis fix in Sidebar.logic, which f5 has. It does not touch the declined Working section.

topics.summary: An inactive working or monitoring thread recedes even with a leftover unread or wake flag. Active, selected, ready, approval and input rows keep full emphasis.
topics.title: Background working threads stay muted in the sidebar

suggestion.reason: Measured performance improvement when opening threads with many images.

topics.summary: Mounted user rows request their own signed image URLs instead of ChatView requesting URLs for every image in the history. In upstream's measurements, initial requests dropped from as many as 3,000 to 15.
topics.title: Threads request image URLs only for mounted rows

suggestion.reason: Fixes a model picker classification bug for a Codex model that f5 users can see.

topics.summary: Adds gpt-6-astra to currentModels.codex in the model manifest, so the picker no longer files it under Legacy models.
topics.title: GPT-6-Astra listed as a current Codex model

topics.summary: Panel animations are suppressed through the first painted frame of the initial load and of each pathname navigation. Restoring thread-specific panel state no longer replays the toggle motion, and explicit toggles still animate.
topics.title: Panels no longer animate when switching threads

suggestion.reason: Measured performance improvement, if f5 runs an equivalent process monitor.

topics.summary: The native monitor on Linux reads command lines, memory and I/O only for selected processes and releases those handles after each sample, which lowers sampling cost.
topics.title: Linux resource monitor reads process details only for tracked processes
